title: Destroy Sequential Targets
summary: Given a 0-indexed array of positive integers and an integer space, find the smallest value in the array that can destroy the most targets, where a target can be destroyed if its value is nums[i] + c * space for any non-negative integer c.
statement: Given a 0-indexed array of positive integers and an integer space, find the smallest value in the array that can destroy the most targets, where a target can be destroyed if its value is nums[i] + c * space for any non-negative integer c.
constraints: Choosing seed x destroys every target equal to x+c*space for a non-negative integer c.
The optimal seed must be one of the array values.
Maximize destroyed occurrences, then return the smallest seed attaining that maximum.
hints: Targets reachable from one seed all have the same remainder modulo space.
Count occurrences in each remainder class.
Find the largest class size and choose the smallest array value belonging to such a class.
A smaller same-remainder seed reaches every larger class member, so class size is the exact achievable count and the final minimum applies the tie break.
editorial: A smaller same-remainder seed reaches every larger class member, so class size is the exact achievable count and the final minimum applies the tie break.

tests.explanation: All odd values share one remainder class, so choosing the smallest odd seed 1 destroys five targets.
Each value is alone in its remainder class, so the smallest value 2 wins the tie.
